precepts.text: But the heathen of the land, lying heavy upon the inhabitants of Judea, and holding them strait, hindered their building; and by their secret plots, and popular persuasions and commotions, they hindered the finishing of the building all the time that king Cyrus lived: so they were hindered from building for the space of two years, until the reign of Darius. See that: secret plots, persuading the multitude against them, causing commotions.
precepts.point: This people say, The time is not come, the time that the Lord's house should be built. Why were they saying that? Everybody was discouraged with the other nations hindering them; they said, maybe this is not the time for the temple to be built. This is why it is important, brothers, to read your four chapters a day; captains, make sure your soldiers are reading, so they can graduate properly by the end of the year having read the whole Bible.
precepts.why:
Haggai brings the word to Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the high priest: “This people say, The time is not come, the time that the Lord’s house should be built.” Why were they saying that? First Esdras shows what was happening: “But the heathen of the land lying heavy upon the inhabitants of Judea, and holding them strait, hindered their building”.

They were hindering the building of the temple. “And by their secret plots, and popular persuasions and commotions, they hindered the finishing of the building all the time that king Cyrus lived: so they were hindered from building for the space of two years, until the reign of Darius.” See that: secret plots, persuading the multitude to go against us, causing commotions.

So everybody was discouraged, with all the other nations hindering them, and they said, maybe this is not the time for the temple to be built. Zerubbabel and Joshua stopped building. Then God raised up Haggai and Zechariah to blast the high priest and the governor so they would go back to the work, and they finished it in the sixth year of the reign of Darius.

That is why it is important to read your four chapters a day. Captains, make sure your soldiers are reading, so they graduate properly at the end of the year having read the whole Bible; then you know the history behind a verse like Haggai 1:2. And the lesson stands for us: the enemy's plots are no reason to let the Lord's house lie waste while we dwell in our cieled houses.

precepts.text: Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates? If you do not know Christ is in you, you are reprobate. That is what all of us have to do: examine ourselves day by day.
precepts.point: Now therefore thus saith the Lord of hosts; Consider your ways. You know what consider your ways means? Examine yourself. And do not say that is only for Zerubbabel; it is not.
precepts.why:
Haggai says, “Now therefore thus saith the Lord of hosts; Consider your ways.” Do you know what consider your ways means? Examine yourself. Paul says it: “Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?”

If you don't know Christ is in you, you are reprobate. That is what all of us have to do: examine ourselves day by day. And don't say consider your ways was only for Zerubbabel; it is not.

Haggai shows what happens when we don't. “Ye have sown much, and bring in little”: you worked a lot with little profit to show for it. “Ye eat, but ye have not enough ... and he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes.” I just worked 48, 52 hours, and I don't have enough money to show for it. That was going on with Zerubbabel, and it is why many of us are always struggling: because God is second or third in your life, just like Zerubbabel. “Because of mine house that is waste, and ye run every man unto his own house.”

When Zerubbabel and Joshua heard it, they “obeyed the voice of the Lord their God, and the words of Haggai the prophet”. Haggai was not governor or high priest, but they humbled themselves, because they knew it was the word of the Lord. They did not say, arrest him. That is how we have to be. When we correct a brother he takes it personal, like we stabbed his mama; correct his wife and he says you are trying to destroy my marriage. No, we are trying to help. That's love. Examine yourself and fix your life.

precepts.text: Is it time for you to dwell in your ceiled houses, and the house of the Lord lie waste? Now is not the time to build your own house first.
precepts.point: I have put my words in thy mouth; I have set thee over the nations and over the kingdoms, to root out, pull down, destroy and throw down, to build and to plant. Shake off the low self-esteem: the Black man has the strength to build brothers and sisters and to prophesy the destruction of these nations.
precepts.why:
The Lord told Jeremiah, “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.” God sent Jeremiah with a purpose. But Jeremiah felt he was too young, that it was not the time: “Ah, Lord God! behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child.”

Some of us think the same way, that now is not the time. That is what Haggai answered: is it time for you to dwell in your ceiled houses, and the house of the Lord lie waste? Now is not the time to build your own house first. What about the house of the Lord?

The Lord did not accept Jeremiah's excuse: “Say not, I am a child: for thou shalt go to all that I shall send thee, and whatsoever I command thee thou shalt speak.” That is a commandment. Jeremiah did not have a choice; it was his from birth. It is the same for you and me: we were ordained from birth to do this work. God knows who you are and did not make a mistake calling you in here. Whatever weakness is in you is no coincidence, and neither is the seat you sit in. Ask yourself why you are here and not dead in the world.

So do not doubt yourself, and do not let Satan take the prize from you. Maybe it feels like too much work; just do it. Put the Lord's house before your own, and speak what we are commanded: Christ is a black man, sent to the twelve tribes of the house of Israel.

“Who is left among you that saw this house in her first glory? and how do ye see it now? is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing?” You would have to be very old: they had been away seventy years. Who still alive remembers the temple Solomon built, before Babylon destroyed it? Compared with what Solomon built, what they were building was nothing.

Yet: “be strong, O Zerubbabel, saith the Lord; and be strong, O Joshua, son of Josedech, the high priest; and be strong, all ye people of the land, saith the Lord, and work: for I am with you”.

“The elders of the Jews builded, and they prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo.” Not only Haggai but Zechariah was prophesying to them. “And they builded, and finished it”, “and this house was finished on the third day of the month Adar, which was in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king.” Adar is the twelfth month, February. The second temple was rebuilt.

points: In the second year of Darius the king came the word of the Lord by Haggai the prophet unto Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest.

This people say, The time is not come, the time that the Lord's house should be built. Why were they saying that? Everybody was discouraged with the other nations hindering them; they said, maybe this is not the time for the temple to be built. This is why it is important, brothers, to read your four chapters a day; captains, make sure your soldiers are reading, so they can graduate properly by the end of the year having read the whole Bible.

Is it time for you, O ye, to dwell in your cieled houses, and this house lie waste? Hey Zerubbabel, is it time for you to live in your nice house with the new roof, while the Lord's house is a shambles?
Now therefore thus saith the Lord of hosts; Consider your ways. You know what consider your ways means? Examine yourself. And do not say that is only for Zerubbabel; it is not.

Ye have sown much, and bring in little: you have worked a lot with little profit to show for it. Ye eat, but ye have not enough; ye drink, but ye are not filled with drink; ye clothe you, but there is none warm; and he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes. I just worked 48, 52 hours and I do not have enough money to show for it. Not only was that going on with Zerubbabel: that is why many of us in here are always struggling, because God is always second or third in your life, just like Zerubbabel.
Go up to the mountain, and bring wood, and build the house; and I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified, saith the Lord.

Ye looked for much, and, lo, it came to little; and when ye brought it home, I did blow upon it. Why? saith the Lord of hosts. Because of mine house that is waste, and ye run every man unto his own house. You are not looking after God's house first.

Therefore the heaven over you is stayed from dew, and the earth is stayed from her fruit: you are not getting blessings in your crops. And I called for a drought upon the land, and upon the mountains, and upon the corn, and upon the new wine, and upon the oil, and upon men, and upon cattle, and upon all the labour of the hands.

Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Joshua the son of Josedech the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of the Lord their God, and the words of Haggai the prophet, and the people did fear before the Lord.

Notice: Joshua was the high priest, Zerubbabel was the governor; Haggai was not in those positions. But Joshua and Zerubbabel humbled themselves, because they knew it was the word of the Lord; they knew Haggai and Zechariah were sent of God. Zerubbabel could have said, arrest him, lock him up; or he could have punched a hole in his chest. He did none of that. He said, I recognize the word of the Lord; I am going to humble myself.

Then spake Haggai the Lord's messenger in the Lord's message unto the people, saying, I am with you, saith the Lord. And the Lord stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel, and the spirit of Joshua, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people; and they came and did work in the house of the Lord of hosts, their God.

Is it time for you, O ye, to dwell in your cieled houses, and this house lie waste: this house is talking about, in context, the temple of the Lord that was supposed to be being rebuilt by the remnant that was allowed to return to rebuild it. But what was that remnant doing? They ass was on vacation. They were chilling in the crib.

Consider your ways: cuz they had excuses. Well, a couple years ago, Darius, and a couple years ago they made a law that we couldn't, they stopped the funding. No. What about right now, today? Lord said, consider your ways.

So you hear that verse, your first thought is excuses, man. Cuz I ain't get this raise, and I tried, and I was applying, and the prices went up on this and that, and I got this ticket that came out of nowhere. What is God reply to all of that? Thus saith the LORD of hosts; Consider your ways. That's God response to you, black man and black woman.

Consider your way. Track your actions and own your results. It's you. You the reason why you at the dead end job. You the reason why you still in an apartment and out the house. Take accountability. Consider your ways. What are you doing or not doing that can change your results? That's accountability, brothers and sisters. Major key of discipline.

Ye have sown much, and bring in little: you work, but it ain't enough. You ain't bringing in enough. Ye eat, but ye have not enough: you not full, you should be. Ye clothe you, but there is none warm: you don't have enough clothing.

And he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes: you get money, but it's like it just go in one pocket and never come back out the pocket. It go through the pocket. The hell is this? What's going on? The bag never increase.

In the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, in the first day of the month, came the word of the Lord by Haggai the prophet unto Zerubbabel the governor of Judah, and to Joshua the high priest.
This people say, The time is not come, the time that the Lord's house should be built.
Is it time for you, O ye, to dwell in your cieled houses, and this house lie waste?
Now therefore thus saith the Lord of hosts; Consider your ways.

Ye have sown much, and bring in little; ye eat, but ye have not enough; ye drink, but ye are not filled with drink; ye clothe you, but there is none warm; and he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes.
Go up to the mountain, and bring wood, and build the house; and I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified, saith the Lord.

Ye looked for much, and lo, it came to little; and when ye brought it home, I did blow upon it. Why? saith the Lord of hosts. Because of mine house that is waste, and ye run every man unto his own house.
Therefore the heaven over you is stayed from dew, and the earth is stayed from her fruit. And I called for a drought upon the land, and upon all the labour of the hands.

Then Zerubbabel, and Joshua the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of the Lord their God, and the words of Haggai the prophet, as the Lord their God had sent him; and the people did fear before the Lord.
Then spake Haggai the Lord's messenger in the Lord's message unto the people, saying, I am with you, saith the Lord.

The Lord stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel, and the spirit of Joshua the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people; and they came and did work in the house of the Lord of hosts, their God.

What happened in those two years? “In the second year of Darius the king” the word came by Haggai to Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the high priest: “This people say, The time is not come, the time that the Lord’s house should be built.” They were saying that because of the secret plots, popular persuasions and commotions that hindered them.

“Is it time for you, O ye, to dwell in your cieled houses, and this house lie waste?” God did not send Haggai to play with them. You are a governor, you are a high priest, you live lovely in your homes, but look at God’s house: you haven’t put a brick to it.

“Consider your ways. Ye have sown much, and bring in little; ye eat, but ye have not enough”, “and he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes.” Everything you have, you are going to lose; you have been losing it, and now I am telling you why.
“Go up to the mountain, and bring wood, and build the house; and I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified, saith the Lord.”

“When ye brought it home, I did blow upon it. Why? saith the Lord of hosts. Because of mine house that is waste, and ye run every man unto his own house.” God himself blew on what they brought home. Some of us can relate: we work for Esau or have our own businesses, we bring in little, and we are confused why things keep going wrong. It is because you are not putting your bricks in here.

“The heaven over you is stayed from dew, and the earth is stayed from her fruit”: no blessings from heaven or earth, and a drought on the land, the corn, the wine, the oil, men, cattle and all the labour of the hands.

“Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of the Lord their God, and the words of Haggai the prophet”. They did not say, I am over you. They took heed, because they knew it was the word of the Lord. “I am with you, saith the Lord.” And the Lord stirred up their spirits, “and they came and did work in the house of the Lord of hosts”.
